messages:
maya: quick heads-up — noticed the Python SDK is serializing request params differently than the REST contract; example: SDK sends { 'top_k': 5, 'retries': None } but the router expects { 'topK': 5 } and omits nulls. this causes validation errors when hitting the hosted endpoint. reproducible on staging.
aj: saw this in the e2e run earlier. failing request log snippet:
```
POST /v1/infer
{ "top_k": 5, "n": 1 }
```
server response: 400 validation error — unknown field 'top_k'. :grimacing:
ben: hmm — iirc the TS SDK runs a transform pipeline that camelCases keys before sending. does py have an equivalent? :eyes:
maya: not currently. py sdk uses dataclasses + asdict so keys stay snake_case. quick mitigation is to have the serializer camelCase top-level keys and drop None values on export. that would match the contract but is a behavioral change.
aj: minimal patch plan — only apply camelCase + drop-nulls for outbound REST payloads (keep internal model shape unchanged). add an integration test verifying request JSON matches contract. also add a small compatibility flag so existing callers relying on snake_case can opt-in while we roll out.
dev-bot: contract-tests failed on PR #4123: tests/contract/test_param_casing.py::test_topk_casing — see CI logs.
maya: ok i'll draft a PR tonight: py-sdk serializer change (camelize keys + remove None fields) + env var REDWOOD_PY_SDK_LEGACY=true to preserve old behavior for one release. assigning @aj for review. :+1:
ben: suggestion — call the env var REDWOOD_PY_SDK_COMPAT_MODE to be clearer. include changelog note and mark as semver-minor.
aj: sounds good. ping me when draft is ready, i'll run the contract suite locally before merging.
maya: ETA PR in ~3h. thanks! :pray:
